Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination—Partial Knee Replacement  
Member: Reese Mercado  
Member ID: W529317483  
Plan: Cigna Commercial/ACA—Arizona  
Reference number: POC-8AD74FF769-66861  
Requested service: Partial knee replacement  
CPT: 27446  
Date of denial notice: August 1, 2026  

Dear Cigna Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing Cigna’s denial of prior authorization for my partial knee replacement. The denial states that the submitted imaging does not support medical necessity. The clinical records, particularly the MRI dated June 8, 2026, directly establish severe, isolated medial-compartment disease and support the requested procedure.

The Cigna policy document identified for this service is CMM-311: Knee Replacement/Arthroplasty. The retrieved policy text states:

“Partial Knee Replacement - Unicompartmental (Medial, Lateral, or Patellofemoral).”

It further states:

“Partial knee replacement (medial, lateral, or patellofemoral) is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:”

The imaging portion of the retrieved policy states:

“Imaging or arthroscopic findings show EITHER of the following:”

and identifies:

“severe unicompartmental (medial, lateral, or patellofemoral) osteoarthritis.”

My June 8, 2026 MRI meets this imaging requirement. It documents full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medial osteoarthritis. These findings demonstrate severe disease concentrated in the medial compartment—the same compartment addressed by a medial unicompartmental knee replacement. Accordingly, the imaging does support medical necessity under the quoted policy criterion.

The remaining clinical record also supports the need for surgery:

- I have experienced 24 months of progressive knee pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- I completed 8 weeks and 24 visits of supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, from May 12, 2026, through July 7, 2026, without adequate relief.
- I used NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate benefit.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 18, 2026, provided only 3 weeks of partial relief.
- I cannot climb stairs without assistance.
- Pain wakes me 3 to 4 times each night.
- Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.
- I have no active infection or untreated substance-use condition, have a BMI of 29, and am a nonsmoker.

These records show severe structural medial-compartment disease, persistent symptoms despite appropriate conservative treatment, and substantial functional impairment. The MRI is not merely suggestive of mild or nonspecific degeneration; it documents full-thickness cartilage loss, bone-on-bone contact, and grade 4 medial osteoarthritis.

Please overturn the denial and approve CPT 27446. If Cigna maintains the denial, please provide the specific clinical-review rationale explaining why the documented MRI findings—full-thickness medial-compartment cartilage loss, bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medial osteoarthritis—do not satisfy the applicable medical-necessity criteria. Please also provide the complete policy and case-specific criteria relied upon in the determination.

I authorize my treating surgeon, Lindqvist, MD, and the orthopedic surgery office to provide additional information and discuss this appeal with Cigna. Please review the enclosed records, including the MRI report, physical therapy discharge note, medication and injection history, examination findings, and the surgeon’s clinical documentation.

This appeal is submitted within the 180-day appeal period stated in the denial notice and must be received no later than January 28, 2027.

Sincerely,

Reese Mercado  
Member ID: W529317483
